# **Global Privacy Policy** ## Who We Are Incorta, Inc. (“Incorta”, “we”, “us”, or “our”) is a business analytics software company headquartered in San Mateo, California, United States. We provide a unified data and analytics platform that enables organizations to connect, ingest, enrich, analyze, and visualize enterprise data in real time. Our platform is designed to help businesses simplify complex data environments and empower users to gain insights without the need for traditional data modeling or transformation. This Global Privacy Notice applies to personal data collected and processed by Incorta and its affiliated entities globally, including through: - Our websites (e.g., [www.incorta.com](https://www.incorta.com/)) - Our software-as-a-service (SaaS) offerings (e.g., Incorta Cloud) - Our mobile applications - Customer support services - Marketing campaigns and communications - Events and business development interactions For the purposes of the General Data Protection Regulation (“GDPR”), Incorta acts as a **data controller** when we determine the purposes and means of processing personal data—such as when we collect data from website visitors, subscribers, prospects, or event participants. When our customers use the Incorta platform to process their own data, Incorta acts as a **data processor**, and our customers are the data controllers of that data. If you have questions about this Privacy Notice or how we handle personal data, please contact us at: **Incorta, Inc.** 2755 Campus Drive, Suite 350 San Mateo, CA 94403 United States Email: [privacy@incorta.com](mailto:privacy@incorta.com) Phone: +1 (650) 242-1210 Our Data Protection Officer is Privaon Oy. The DPO represents Incorta in matters relating to data protection compliance, data subject requests, complaint resolution, and risk mitigation. You may contact the DPO by emailing [privacy@incorta.com](mailto:privacy@incorta.com) with the subject line "DPO Inquiry," or by submitting a request via our [**Data Subject Request Form.**](https://app.dpo365.com/forms?businessId=b0160&formTemplateId=03b4b27d-4f33-41aa-83f8-cb965c95fe29&formId=943760ea-38e1-4375-b2f7-27291c5b83de) ### Lead Supervisory Authority The Finnish Office of the Data Protection Ombudsman serves as Incorta’s lead supervisory authority under the GDPR, based on our main establishment in the European Union. For individuals located in Finland, the competent supervisory authority is: - Office of the Data Protection Ombudsman (Tietosuojavaltuutetun toimisto) - P.O. Box 800 - 00531 Helsinki - Finland - Email: [tietosuoja@om.fi](mailto:tietosuoja@om.fi) - Telephone: +358 29 566 6700 - Website: [www.tietosuoja.fi](https://www.tietosuoja.fi/) Contacting our DPO does not limit your right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority. You may also contact the supervisory authority in the country where you normally live, where you work, or where the alleged infringement of data protection law has taken place. A directory of EU supervisory authorities is available at [https://edpb.europa.eu/about-edpb/board/members\_en](https://edpb.europa.eu/about-edpb/board/members_en). ## Scope and Purpose of This Global Privacy Notice Incorta, Inc. (“ **Incorta**”) understands that your privacy matters, and we are committed to protecting the personal information of individuals who interact with us. This Global Privacy Notice describes how Incorta and its affiliated entities (“Incorta”) collect, use, and protect personal information through our websites, services, and applications. The term ‘Personal Information’ is used throughout this Privacy Notice to refer to personal data as defined under applicable data protection and privacy laws, including the GDPR and U.S. state privacy laws. This Global Privacy Notice also details our privacy practices related to Incorta marketing, advertising, and company events. Incorta is a business analytics platform. We provide Incorta Services (“ **Services**”) and related support, consulting, and other services to our customers. We collectively refer to our emails, newsletters, and other marketing practices as our Communications (“ **Communications**”). This Privacy Notice applies to individuals whose personal data we process as a controller, including website visitors, prospects, customers, event participants, and users of our services, in accordance with applicable laws such as the **General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)** and the **California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA)**. ## What This Privacy Notice Covers - Our websites (e.g., incorta.com) - Mobile applications - SaaS analytics platform (Incorta Cloud) - Marketing emails and newsletters - Event registration and participation - Customer support services Please note: This policy does not apply to services or components of our platform governed by a separate Privacy Notice or where we act as a data processor on behalf of our customers. In those cases, your data is subject to your organization’s Privacy Notice. ## Incorta Services and Our Role in Data Processing ### Overview of Incorta Services Incorta Cloud is our cloud-based unified data analytics platform that enables customers to connect and analyze complex data in real time. It includes features for data ingestion, enrichment, visualization, and sharing—eliminating the need for traditional data modeling or transformation. We also offer a range of related services that support our platform and customers’ data strategies, including: - Platform implementation and onboarding - Technical support and customer success services - Training programs, webinars, and documentation - Solution consulting and custom configuration - Access to updates, new features, and release notes These services may involve the processing of personal data when users interact with our platform, contact our support teams, register for events, or access resources. When we process personal information for these purposes, we do so in accordance with applicable data protection/ privacy laws and the principles outlined in this Privacy Notice. ### Customer Data When customers use Incorta’s Services, they may upload or store data within our platform. This Customer Data is owned and controlled by the customer. Incorta only processes this data on behalf of and under the instruction of our customers. #### What is Customer Data? - Data uploaded, stored, or processed through the Incorta Cloud platform - Controlled by the customer (the data controller) - May include personal information of individuals known to the customer (e.g., employees, clients) - Incorta does not use this data for its own purposes ### Our Role as Data Processor In these circumstances, Incorta acts as a data processor, and our responsibilities are governed by: - The contractual terms agreed upon with each customer - The customer’s own Privacy Notice - Applicable data protection laws, including Article 28 of the GDPR We follow these core principles when handling Customer Data: - We process data only on documented instructions from the customer - We implement appropriate technical and organizational safeguards - We assist customers in meeting their compliance obligations where applicable - We do not access or use Customer Data for marketing or analytics unrelated to the Services Details of our processing obligations are set out in our Data Processing Agreement, which is available upon request at [privacy@incorta.com](mailto:privacy@incorta.com). ## Privacy Principles ### Fair and Lawful Processing Incorta processes personal data on one or more of the following legal bases, as defined under the GDPR and equivalent privacy laws: - Consent (Art. 6(1)(a)): Where you have given clear affirmative consent — for example, to receive marketing communications, to allow non-essential cookies, or to process special category data. - Contract (Art. 6(1)(b)): Where processing is necessary to enter into or perform a contract with you or your organization, including delivery of the Incorta Services, account administration, and support. - Legal obligation (Art. 6(1)(c)): Where processing is required to comply with applicable laws and regulations, such as tax, accounting, employment, anti-fraud, or law-enforcement obligations. - Legitimate interests (Art. 6(1)(f)): Where processing is necessary for our or a third party's legitimate interests, provided those interests are not overridden by your rights and freedoms. We rely on legitimate interests for activities such as: improving and securing our Services, conducting product analytics on aggregated or pseudonymized data, managing direct B2B communications with prospective customers, detecting and preventing fraud or abuse, and exercising or defending legal claims. We conduct a Legitimate Interests Assessment (LIA) before relying on this basis. - Vital interests or public interest (Art. 6(1)(d)–(e)): Only in narrow circumstances, such as responding to a security incident affecting the safety of individuals. Processing of **special category data** (Art. 9) is carried out only where an additional condition applies, such as your explicit consent, compliance with employment or social-security obligations, or the establishment, exercise, or defense of legal claims. ### Transparency and Purpose Limitations We are committed to transparency about the Personal Information we collect and how we use it. Where required, we provide individuals with a clear notice at the point of collection and obtain consent for data uses when necessary. We collect data only: - For **specified, explicit, and legitimate purposes** - In a way that is **relevant and proportionate** to the purpose - With the intent to **minimize the amount** of Personal Information we collect and retain. We do **not use** Personal Information in ways that are incompatible with the original purposes disclosed, unless we notify you and, where necessary, obtain your consent. ### Consent In certain situations, we rely on your consent to collect and process your personal information. For example, we request your consent when: - You sign up for our marketing Communications (e.g., newsletters, product updates) - You provide sensitive information/special category data (e.g., health info for event accommodations) - You interact with our Services where optional data collection is involved (e.g., webinars, optional profile fields). Note that the use of cookies and similar tracking technologies on our websites is separately governed by the ePrivacy Directive (and equivalent national implementations) and is addressed in detail in our Cookies Notice. Where we rely on your consent, you can withdraw it at any time by using the opt-out mechanisms provided in our communications, cookie settings, or by contacting us directly, via this form on our website [https://www.incorta.com/contact](https://www.incorta.com/contact). ## Types of Personal Information We Collect The following table outlines the categories of personal data Incorta may collect, along with examples and typical sources of collection: | Category | Description / Examples | How It’s Collected | Legal Basis | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Demographic & Contact Info | Name, email address, phone number, company name, job title, country or region | Web forms, event registrations, sales inquiries | Consent, Contract | | Account & Login Details | Username, password, email address, MFA preferences, security questions | Account registration, login activity | Contract, Legitimate Interest | | Device & Technical Info | IP address, browser type/version, operating system, device ID, time zone, language.
Note: where required by law analytics and tracking technologies are only activated after consent is obtained | Automatically via browser or device | Legitimate Interest | | Website Interaction Data | Pages viewed, session duration, clicks, error logs, referring URLs, heatmaps | Cookies, analytics tools (e.g., Google Analytics, Wistia) | Consent (for non-essential cookies) | | Location Data | IP-based location, selected region or country, GPS location (if enabled).
Note: GPS collection is optional and user controlled. | Automatically via device/browser; app permissions | Consent, Legitimate Interest | | Financial & Transaction Data | Cardholder name, billing address, payment type, purchase amount/history | Through secure third-party payment providers | Contract, Legal Obligation | | Communication Preferences | Email opt-in/out, subscription types, marketing interactions, survey responses | Newsletter sign-ups, feedback forms, preference centers | Consent | | Event & Webinar Data | Name, company, contact info, session attendance, accessibility requests | Registration forms, participation logs, post-event surveys | Consent, Legitimate Interest | | Social Media Interactions | Public comments, likes, shares, social handle or profile name | Interactions on platforms (LinkedIn, X/Twitter, etc.) | Consent, Publicly Available Data | | Customer Support Data | Chat transcripts, email threads, support tickets, screenshots, technical logs | Help center, support forms, product feedback submissions | Contract, Legitimate Interest | | Sensitive Personal Information | Health data (e.g., dietary or accessibility info), government ID (where required) | Explicitly provided by user only when necessary | Explicit Consent, Legal Obligation.
Note: we do not use Sensitive Personal Information to infer characteristics. | ## How We Collect Personal Information Incorta collects personal information in several ways depending on how you interact with our websites, mobile apps, communications, and services. We gather this information to deliver services, support business operations, fulfill legal obligations, and improve user experience. This section outlines the primary sources and types of information we collect. **We may collect personal data from the following sources:** ### Webforms and Requests When you submit information to us through webforms, such as “Contact Us,” demo requests, support inquiries, newsletter signups, or resource downloads—we collect the information you provide, including your name, email, company name, phone number, and any message or additional details you choose to include. You may also submit requests to exercise your data rights (such as access or deletion), in which case we will process the information needed to verify and fulfill your request. ### Website Browsing Activity When you visit our websites (such as [www.incorta.com](https://www.incorta.com/)), we automatically collect certain information about your device and usage through cookies and other tracking technologies. This includes: - IP address - Browser type and version - Operating system - Referring/exit pages - Date and time of access - Clickstream data - Pages viewed and actions taken - Session duration and interactions This information is used to optimize our site performance, security, and marketing effectiveness. For more details, see: [Cookies and Tracking Technologies](https://www.incorta.com/legal-pages/global-privacy-policy#cookies-and-tracking-technologies). ### Device Information and Log Data We may collect technical information from the devices you use to access our services. This includes: - Device type and model - Operating system version - Unique device identifiers (e.g., MAC address, advertising ID) - Network and connection information - Log files and error reports Where technically feasible, unique device identifiers are hashed or otherwise pseudonymized before being stored in our systems. If you use multiple devices to access your Incorta account, we may associate sessions across those devices solely to support secure authentication, session continuity, and fraud detection. We do not use cross-device linking to build behavioral profiles or to make automated decisions that produce legal or similarly significant effects on you. ### Mobile Applications and Social Media Some of our services are accessible via mobile apps or mobile-optimized sites. When you use these channels, we may collect: - Mobile device ID - Device location (based on GPS or IP) - App interaction data - Mobile OS version and platform In addition, we maintain company pages on platforms such as LinkedIn, Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, YouTube, Vimeo, and others. If you interact with our content or submit information through those platforms (e.g., likes, comments, messages), that data may be collected by both us and the platform provider, subject to their privacy policies. ### Location Data Depending on your device settings and the features you use, we may collect location data to tailor content or comply with local laws. This may include: - General location inferred from your IP address - Precise GPS-based location (if enabled on mobile) - Location preferences you select on our Services You can manage or disable location collection through your browser, device settings, or app permissions. ### Business Interactions and Transactions We may collect information about you and your company through direct business interactions, such as: - Meetings or phone calls - Tradeshow or event attendance - Partner referrals - Contract discussions or negotiations This may include your name, title, company name, business email and phone number, job role, and other information relevant to the business relationship. ### Financial Information If you purchase services or software from us, we may collect payment-related information such as: - Name on card - Billing address - Card type and expiration - Transaction date and amount This data is securely processed through trusted third-party payment providers and is not stored by Incorta directly unless necessary for legal or contractual compliance. ### Events and Webinars If you register for one of our in-person events or online webinars, we may collect: - Your name, title, and contact details - Company name and role - Session attendance data - Feedback or survey responses This information may be used to follow up on your interest, respond to your inquiries, and improve future event offerings. ### Communications and Subscriptions If you sign up to receive marketing communications, newsletters, product updates, or other promotional content, we collect your name and email address, as well as preferences or interaction data related to those communications (e.g., email open/click rates). From time to time, we may provide electronic or printed communications to our customers and prospective customers. These communications may include updates about our products, services, company news, offers, and events. If you subscribe, you will be added to our mailing list and receive communications at the contact information you provide. In some cases, our Services may allow us or other users to contact you via text message (SMS). These messages may include service notifications, system alerts, or other service-related communications. You can manage your notification preferences, including opting out of text messages, through your account settings or by contacting us. We request your consent before using your personal information for marketing purposes, including email and SMS. You may withdraw your consent at any time using the opt-out instructions in the message or by contacting us directly. Your name and email address may be stored in a third-party mailing system based in the United States or Europe. These providers are contractually obligated to follow appropriate data protection standards. We do not use your information for automated decision-making. We retain your communication preferences and contact data for as long as we continue sending communications. If you unsubscribe, we promptly suppress your contact details from active marketing lists. We retain a minimum set of suppression data (typically your email address in hashed form, the date you unsubscribed, and the source of the original opt-in) for up to three years solely to honor your opt-out choice, prevent re-contact, and demonstrate compliance with applicable anti-spam and data protection laws (including CAN-SPAM, the GDPR, and the ePrivacy Directive). Suppression data is not used for any marketing or analytics purpose. After three years, we securely delete the suppression record unless a longer period is required by law. You may withdraw consent or opt out of further processing at any time by: - Clicking the "Unsubscribe" link in any marketing email - Replying "STOP" to SMS communications - Adjusting your preferences in the cookie consent manager on our website - Emailing [privacy@incorta.com](mailto:privacy@incorta.com) - Submitting a request through our [**Data Subject Request Form.**](https://app.dpo365.com/forms?businessId=b0160&formTemplateId=03b4b27d-4f33-41aa-83f8-cb965c95fe29&formId=943760ea-38e1-4375-b2f7-27291c5b83de) We will action verified opt-out requests without undue delay and within the timeframes required by applicable law. ### Personal Data Obtained from Third-Party Sources In addition to information you provide directly, we may receive personal data about you from the following third-party sources: - **Your employer or organization:** Where your employer is an Incorta customer, your employer may provide your contact details, role, and access credentials so we can provision the Services to you. - **Your authorized representatives:** Where you have authorized an agent, advisor, or representative to act on your behalf, we may receive your information from them. - **Business partners and resellers:** Channel partners, integrators, and resellers may share your business contact details where they have a lawful basis to do so. - **Event and webinar co-sponsors:** Where Incorta co-hosts an event, we may receive registration details from the co-sponsor, subject to the disclosures made at registration. - **Publicly available sources:** Such as professional networking platforms (e.g., LinkedIn), corporate websites, and public registries, where consistent with the source platform's terms. - **Analytics, advertising, and marketing technology providers:** Who may share aggregated or pseudonymized data relating to your interactions with our digital properties. - **Service providers and subprocessors:** Acting on Incorta's behalf in support of our operations. We require third parties who provide personal data to us to have a lawful basis for doing so and to have provided any required notices to the individuals concerned. ## How We Use and Share Your Information ### How We Share Personal Information In accordance with applicable data protection laws and industry standards, Incorta does not share personal information with third parties unless they provide at least the same level of protection as this Privacy Notice requires. We may share Personal Information with: - Vetted service providers and subprocessors that support our operations (e.g., hosting, CRM, analytics, marketing tools) - Affiliated Incorta entities under a common data protection framework - Regulatory or legal authorities, when required by law - Partners and resellers, if necessary to support customer relationships or services In addition, we may share your personal information: - With your consent, where required by law or when appropriate for specific purposes - To prevent or respond to fraud, security threats, or potential harm - In connection with a merger, acquisition, reorganization, or sale of assets, where your data may be transferred as part of the transaction - In de-identified or aggregated form that cannot reasonably be used to identify you, for statistical analysis or business intelligence - With third-party messaging or communication service providers, such as SMS carriers or email platforms, where necessary to deliver communications All third parties who process data on our behalf are required to sign Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) that include obligations under Article 28 of the GDPR and CCPA’s service provider rules. **We do not sell personal information for monetary or other valuable consideration.** ### Sharing of De-Identified or Aggregated Data We may use and share aggregated or de-identified information that cannot reasonably be used to identify you. This type of data is used for purposes such as: - Statistical reporting and analytics - Product development and optimization - Industry trend analysis - Internal business insights This data is no longer considered personal information under applicable privacy laws and is not subject to the same restrictions. ### International Transfers of Personal Data We may transfer personal information to countries outside of your home country, including the United States and Egypt, where data protection laws may differ from those in your jurisdiction. To ensure that international transfers comply with applicable laws, we implement one or more of the following safeguards: - Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) approved by the European Commission - Transfer Impact Assessments (TIAs) in line with EDPB guidance (post-Schrems II) - Where applicable, certified participation in approved cross-border transfer frameworks We take appropriate steps to ensure that personal data transferred internationally is protected with adequate and consistent safeguards. If you would like more information about our international transfer mechanisms, please contact us at [privacy@incorta.com](mailto:privacy@incorta.com) ### Automated Decision-Making and Profiling Incorta does not currently use personal information to make decisions based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produce legal effects or similarly significant effects on individuals within the meaning of Article 22 of the GDPR. All decisions that may materially affect individuals involve meaningful human review. If this position changes, for example, as a result of new product features or AI capabilities, Incorta will update this Privacy Notice, and where required by law, will provide individuals with appropriate notice, the safeguards required under Article 22, and the right to obtain human intervention, express their point of view, and contest the decision. ## Your Privacy Rights Incorta respects the privacy rights granted to individuals under applicable data protection and privacy laws. The rights available to you depend on your location and the laws that apply to your personal data. ### European Privacy Rights (EEA, UK, and Switzerland) If you are located in the European Economic Area (EEA), the United Kingdom, or Switzerland, you have the following rights under the GDPR, UK GDPR, and Swiss FADP: - **Right of Access:** Request confirmation of whether we process your personal data and obtain a copy of that data and how it is used. - **Right to Rectification:** Request correction of inaccurate or incomplete personal data. - **Right to Erasure ("Right to Be Forgotten"):** Request deletion of your data when it is no longer necessary, you withdraw consent, you object to processing, or it was processed unlawfully (subject to legal retention obligations). - **Right to Restriction:** Request we limit processing if data accuracy is contested, processing is unlawful, the data is needed for legal claims, or pending verification of an objection. - **Right to Data Portability:** Receive your data in a structured, machine-readable format, or have it transferred to another controller where technically feasible. - **Right to Object:** Object at any time to processing based on legitimate interests (including profiling) or direct marketing. - **Right to Withdraw Consent:** Withdraw previously granted consent at any time (this does not affect processing that occurred prior to withdrawal). - **Right to Lodge a Complaint:**File a complaint with your local data protection authority. - _Incorta’s lead supervisory authority is the Finnish Office of the Data Protection Ombudsman ( [www.tietosuoja.fi](https://www.tietosuoja.fi/)). Contact details for all EU authorities are available via the [European Data Protection Board](https://edpb.europa.eu/about-edpb/board/members_en)._ ### U.S. State Privacy Rights (California and Others) This section applies to residents of California (under the CPRA) and other U.S. states with comprehensive privacy laws (including VA, CO, CT, and UT). Incorta honors these rights in accordance with applicable state laws. Your U.S. Privacy Rights Subject to verification and legal exceptions, you have the right to: - **Know / Access:** Request disclosure of the categories of data collected, sources, purposes of use, third-party sharing, and the specific pieces of data collected about you. - **Delete:** Request deletion of your collected personal information. - **Correct:** Request correction of inaccurate personal information. - **Opt-Out of Sharing / Targeted Advertising:** Opt out of the sharing or sale of personal information for cross-context behavioral advertising. _(Note: Incorta does not sell personal information)._ - **Limit Use of Sensitive Information:** Request limitations on how we use or disclose Sensitive Personal Information. - **Non-Discrimination:** You will not be discriminated against for exercising your privacy rights. ### Categories of Personal Information We Collect For purposes of U.S. state laws, we collect and use the following data for business purposes (including service delivery, security, marketing, and compliance): | Category | Examples of Data Collected | | --- | --- | | Identifiers | Name, email address, IP address, online identifiers. | | Commercial Information | Services purchased, transaction history. | | Network Activity | Website interactions, analytics data. | | Geolocation Data | IP-based location; precise location (only where enabled). | | Professional / Employment | Job title, company name. | | Sensitive Information | Limited strictly to necessary use cases (e.g., accessibility or dietary needs for events). We do not use this data for profiling. | **Global Privacy Control (GPC)** Incorta honors Global Privacy Control (GPC) signals as a valid request to opt out of sharing data for cross-context behavioral advertising. If we detect a GPC signal from your browser or device, we will treat it as an opt-out request for that specific browser/device without requiring further action from you. ### How to Exercise Your Rights You have reasonable access to the Personal Information Incorta holds about you. Whenever possible, you may update your information directly through your Incorta account or profile settings. To formally exercise any of your regional or global privacy rights, you or your authorized agent may contact us using the following methods: - Email: [privacy@incorta.com](mailto:privacy@incorta.com) - Web Form: Submit a request via our [**Data Subject Request Form.**](https://app.dpo365.com/forms?businessId=b0160&formTemplateId=03b4b27d-4f33-41aa-83f8-cb965c95fe29&formId=943760ea-38e1-4375-b2f7-27291c5b83de) - Browser: Enable Global Privacy Control (GPC) in your browser settings (for applicable U.S. residents) Response Timeframes We may verify your identity before processing your request. If a request is denied, you will be informed of the reason and provided with appeal instructions where required by law. | Jurisdiction | Standard Response Time | Permitted Extension | | --- | --- | --- | | **GDPR (Europe)** | 1 Month | Up to 2 additional months (for complex requests) | | **U.S. States** | 45 Days | Up to 45 additional days (with notification to you) | ## Data Retention & Accuracy ### How We Keep Your Data Accurate Incorta makes a good faith effort to ensure that all personal information we process is accurate, complete, and up to date. We collect only the personal data necessary for specified purposes and take reasonable steps to keep it current. Individuals may access or update their information through their user profile or by contacting us at [privacy@incorta.com.](mailto:privacy@incorta.com) ### Our Approach to Retention We retain personal information only as long as necessary to fulfill the purposes for which it was collected, or as required by applicable laws, regulations, and internal business needs. Our retention periods are guided by our formal Records Retention Policy, which groups record types into categories with defined durations based on legal, regulatory, and operational requirements (e.g., financial records, audit logs, customer data, etc.). Once data is no longer required for legal or business purposes, we securely delete, anonymize, or archive it, in accordance with applicable laws and industry standards. You may request deletion of your personal information at any time, subject to our legal and contractual obligations. ### Retention Period Examples The table below provides examples of common data types and general retention periods. Specific durations may vary based on the nature of the data, user agreements, or applicable regulations. ### Data Retention Summary Table | Data Category | General Retention Period | Justification | | --- | --- | --- | | Accounting Records | 7 years | GAAP compliance | | Budgeting/Forecasting | 5 years | Financial planning retention | | System Transaction Logs | 1 year | Backup & recovery (SOC2 alignment) | | Audit Logs | 2 years | Forensic readiness | | Customer Personal Data | 3 years after last activity or contract end | GDPR/CCPA and regulatory compliance | | Supplier/Vendor Data | 3 years after relationship ends | Dispute and compliance period | | Employee Data | 4 years after employment ends | HR compliance / employment law | | Contractual Documents | 7 years after contract ends (or permanent) | Legal limitation periods | | Applicant Data | 2 years | ADA, Civil Rights Act, ADEA | Note: These are general guidelines. In specific cases, data may be retained longer or shorter based on business, legal, or regulatory requirements. ## How We Protect Your Information ### Our Commitment to Data Security Incorta is committed to protecting personal information from unauthorized access, disclosure, alteration, and destruction. We implement and maintain appropriate administrative, technical, and physical security measures aligned with industry standards and legal requirements, including those set out under GDPR and CCPA. Our security approach is regularly reviewed and enhanced as part of our compliance, risk management, and internal audit processes. For data classified as sensitive personal information, we apply additional safeguards in accordance with applicable data protection laws. ### Technical and Organizational Safeguards We apply a multi-layered security model that includes: - Encryption: All data is encrypted at rest and in transit (AES-256 at rest; TLS 1.2 or higher in transit) - Access Controls: Role-based access permissions and least privilege enforcement - Authentication: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for admin-level accounts - Risk Management: Periodic risk assessments and incident response planning - Monitoring: Logging, anomaly detection, and activity monitoring - Infrastructure Hardening: Built on hardened cloud infrastructure (GCP) - Key Management: Enforced policies for key rotation and secure storage - Vendor Security Reviews: Assessments of all processors and sub-processors This is not a comprehensive list of our security controls. For a more detailed overview, you may contact us at [infosec@incorta.com](mailto:infosec@incorta.com). ### Security and Our Service Providers Incorta ensures that any third-party service providers who process personal information on our behalf adhere to equivalent or stronger data protection and security measures. We include contractual safeguards such as data processing agreements and regular compliance checks. Third-party subprocessors are assessed for: - Data access controls - Encryption protocols - Certifications (e.g., ISO 27001, SOC 2) - Breach response procedures We maintain a list of authorized subprocessors, which can be made available upon request. We provide reasonable advance notice of new subprocessors and allow customers to object to changes as set out in our Data Processing Agreement. ### Oversight and Complaint Management If you have concerns or complaints about how your personal information is handled, we encourage you to contact us directly so that we can resolve the issue promptly. - You can reach us at: [privacy@incorta.com](mailto:privacy@incorta.com) - Or by submitting a request via [**our online privacy form**](https://incorta-requests-privacy.my.onetrust.com/webform/9882133f-c1ae-40eb-ae82-1809edb651c1/9c558b5c-5fa6-4a1f-8097-54fbb06e9ab0) Incorta has appointed Privaon Oy as our external Data Protection Officer (DPO) under the GDPR. Privaon Oy represents Incorta in matters relating to data protection compliance, complaint resolution, and risk mitigation. If your concern is unresolved or relates specifically to GDPR compliance, you may contact our DPO using the same contact methods above. Please include “DPO Inquiry” in the subject line if applicable. You also have the right to contact your local data protection authority at any time regarding your privacy rights or concerns. The Finnish Office of the Data Protection Ombudsman serves as Incorta’s lead supervisory authority under the GDPR. To find the contact details for your national supervisory authority, visit: [https://edpb.europa.eu/about-edpb/board/members\_en](https://edpb.europa.eu/about-edpb/board/members_en) ## Cookies and Tracking Technologies ### How We Use Cookies and Similar Technologies When you visit our websites or use our online services, Incorta and third parties may use cookies and other tracking technologies such as web beacons, pixels, tags, and analytics tools to collect and store information about your usage. We use these tools to: - Ensure our websites function properly (strictly necessary cookies) - Measure and improve performance - Personalize content and ads based on your interests - Understand how users interact with our content (e.g., video heatmaps) Some cookies are essential for website operation.
